population.note: FICTIONAL. Off-drug share: ever 41.5% − current 30.8% = 10.7% of adults have used and are off now. 2032 cohort: of the 27.9 then on, 17.3 stayed on (62%, up slightly from 60%). Fewer employer conditioning cut-offs and switching to oral amycretin or Foundayo outweighed the people who lost employer coverage. The other 10.6 stopped and joined the 9.1 already off, a pool of 19.7. Of that pool 10.8 restarted (55%, in line with the parent's 57%), leaving the 2032 cohort at 17.3 + 10.8 = 28.1 on and 19.7 − 10.8 = 8.9 off. New ever-users since 2032 total 41.5 − 37.0 = 4.5, of whom 2.7 are on and 1.8 already off. Totals: on 28.1 + 2.7 = 30.8, off 8.9 + 1.8 = 10.7. Cycled: 13.4 pts who had cycled by 2032, plus ~4.6 first-time restarters and ~0.4 among new starters, give 18.4 of 41.5 ever-users = 44%. Of ~271M adults, ≈83.5M are current users, ≈29.0M have used and stopped, and ≈158.5M have never used. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 3.6 + 10.89 + 11.28 + 5.06 = 30.8. The 65+ band rose 17→22 (≈13.7M of ~62.3M), driven by the dementia-risk label, the unchanged Bridge extension and a pill with no needle. Income thirds: (35 + 31 + 26.4)/3 = 30.8. The top third is saturated. The bottom third rose most (+4.7), and roughly half of that rise is gray-market product, so the counterfeit outbreak landed mainly in this tier. New ever-users slowed from 10.5 pts to 4.5 pts as adoption saturated. Oral parity mostly moved existing users and restarters off the needle rather than recruiting new users. The off-drug population is increasingly people who lost employer coverage in 2033–34 and could not or would not move to cash or gray product. Pediatric: 1.4% of ~73M ≈ 1.02M, of whom ~170k are aged 6–11. A registry-unmeasured fringe of teens on gray pens is reported by school nurses in border counties.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was extended unchanged in the Dec 2033 continuing resolution through Sep 2035. Payment is $225/month with a $50 copay, and continuation still requires ≥5% loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC and annual DEXA plus a resistance-training referral for 65+. Obesity-only Bridge enrolment is ≈4.6M: 4.6M × $225 × 12 ≈ $12.4B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈15.6% of incretin fills ≈ 13.0M users (≈12.4M of the ≈13.7M users aged 65+, plus ~0.6M disabled under-65). The other ~1.3M users aged 65+ pay cash or use gray product. The statutory $225 now exceeds the $199 TrumpRx semaglutide price, an anomaly the CR did not fix. Medicaid pays ≈11.5% ≈ 9.6M users at $225: 9.6M × $225 × 12 ≈ $25.9B/yr combined federal and state. The same seven adherence-waiver states continue (Indiana, Arkansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, Georgia, Ohio, Montana). The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program is flat at $5.0B under CRs for FY2033 and FY2034 and is still unconditional. It serves ≈3.7M: 2.4M generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 = $2.02B, plus 1.3M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $179 × 12 = $2.79B, ≈ $4.81B. TRICARE, the VA and DoD cover ≈2.5M, including ~150k active duty in the Metabolic Readiness Program: 150k × $149 × 12 ≈ $268M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–35/month, and generic tirzepatide is sold in India, Brazil, Turkey, Mexico and Egypt. Generic semaglutide is standard across Canada, Mexico, China and most of Latin America and Asia at $20–60/month. Mexican border-town pharmacies in Reynosa, Nuevo Progreso and Ciudad Juárez sell Mexican-registered generic semaglutide over the counter in practice. Chinese triple agonists are approved domestically. API oversupply has pushed bulk semaglutide prices to a fraction of their 2030 level. In the US, the settlement-licensed 2033 entry date passed with no generic on shelves: the first filer's final approval is blocked by an FDA import alert on its API site and its 180-day exclusivity is parked. Tirzepatide is protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ≈83.5M users: commercial 29.9% (25.0M), Medicare 15.6% (13.0M), Medicaid 11.5% (9.6M), HRSA 4.4% (3.7M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.0% (2.5M), cash/direct 19.9% (16.6M), gray 15.7% (13.1M) = 100%. Managed decline: TrumpRx/direct prices stepped to $199 for semaglutide injection, $249 for tirzepatide, $149 for oral starts and $199 for oral maintenance (Wegovy pill, Foundayo), $279 for oral amycretin (launched Apr 2033) and $299 for retatrutide. Wegovy list is still $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499, and almost nobody pays list. Employer retreat: weight-management coverage fell from 63% to 49% of employers. Remaining commercial coverage is concentrated on type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular, OSA, MASH and AUD codes. Many employers that dropped coverage replaced it with a 'direct access benefit', a manufacturer portal link plus an HSA contribution of $0–600/yr. That counts as access, not coverage. The two tiers are now clear: coded patients with coverage pay $25–50 copays, and weight-only patients pay $149–299 cash or go gray. Gray users rose from ~9.0M to ~13.1M: ~4.0M on 503A compounded product, ~4.0M on cross-border Mexican or Canadian generic, ~2.5M on courier-shipped Indian generic, and ~2.6M, by FDA/CDC estimates, on counterfeit 'US generic' pens that exploit public confusion over the 2033 generic date. Gray prices run $25–120/month. Skip-but-fill persists inside Bridge and the Medicaid waivers but declined as employer adherence conditions disappeared.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular dual agonist, daily oral tablet and weekly injectable (amycretin, Apr 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo; BED low dose 2032; AUD Feb 2034)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, obesity with MASH)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029)
alcohol use disorder (semaglutide, Jun 2030; orforglipron, Feb 2034; first-line option in ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines, 2033–34)
reduction in risk of dementia in adults ≥55 with type 2 diabetes or obesity plus established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, Jun 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'brain health' semaglutide and oral amycretin for 50–65-year-olds outside the dementia label
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
low-dose Foundayo for 'food noise' after brief telehealth BED screens, though the 'quiet' framing has faded
gambling, compulsive shopping and cannabis reduction, still without a label
GLP-1 plus antiresorptive 'bone cover' in 65+, guideline-endorsed
cutting down on drinking without an AUD diagnosis ('moderation dosing') after the orforglipron AUD label
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised through a product that was under review at the start of the step. Novo's 2031 amycretin resubmission covered both the weekly injection and the daily tablet, and FDA approved both in Apr 2033. The oral arm showed 21.8% mean loss at 72 weeks (efficacy estimand), matching tirzepatide's injectable benchmark but not retatrutide 12 mg (30%). Oral peptide needs many times the API of the injection, and Novo pays Section 232 duty on Danish API, so launch supply was rationed through 2033. Oral amycretin had ≈3.4M users by end-2034, mostly switchers. Orforglipron received an AUD supplemental approval (Feb 2034) on a phase 3 heavy-drinking-days endpoint. The bimagrumab + tirzepatide BLA (filed Mar 2032) had its review extended after a major amendment, with action expected 2035, so it is not on the market. MariTide supply expanded to ≈1.6M users. Survodutide remains narrow at ~0.4M. Phase 2 oral triple agonists and Chinese originator molecules are not on the US market. No US generic semaglutide or tirzepatide: the settlement entry date for semaglutide passed in Mar 2033 with the first filer stalled (see events). Global incretin market ≈$178B in 2034: US volume +12% and US net price −12%, with growth mostly ex-US volume at generic prices.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin's GI profile is similar to tirzepatide's during titration. Rates are highest among gray users skipping titration and in counterfeit pens with mislabelled strength.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has grown to ~74,000 filed and tolled claims with no global settlement. A further bellwether split 1–1.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled; FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis; reserves raised again.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases track rapid loss, especially on retatrutide 12 mg.
Registries still show low absolute risk with no causal confirmation. There are case clusters in counterfeit-pen users given unknown doses.

Unchanged population pattern: 65+ users ~0.5 SD below matched non-users in appendicular lean mass. Coaching support dropped out of commercial plans with employer retreat, so cash users now carry most of the unsupported loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings section unchanged; Bridge referral requirement continues; bimagrumab combination still under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose a further ~3% over 2032–33. Modelled excess ≈ 13.7M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr × HR 0.30 (antiresorptive cover tempers it) ≈ 20,500 a year, concentrated in women and cyclers. The adolescent BMD-accrual interim is still unadjudicated. Oral amycretin has no fracture data in 75+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA Warnings unchanged; antiresorptive co-prescription guideline-endorsed; pediatric labelling update still pending the final study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in the BED and AUD populations and in AUD trials of orforglipron.

VA Million Veteran Program and PCORI pragmatic analyses (2033) put validated excess anhedonia at ~3% overall, concentrated at retatrutide ≥8 mg and other doses above maintenance. Survey reports of 'reduced pleasure' fell to ~6–8% of long-term users. The amycretin label lists anhedonia as uncommon. Deliberate dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~28% of long-term users as employer adherence gates disappeared.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide Adverse Reactions and class precaution above maintenance unchanged; FTC 'calm/focus' policing continues at baseline.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now driven by employer retreat as well as conditioning: weight-only users who lost coverage in 2033–34 and did not move to cash or gray product regain on the established curve.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals persist, and are worse among cash and gray users without counselling.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult and eleven of adolescent follow-up. ~170k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still absent. Teen gray-pen use is unmeasured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; bone interim still under FDA review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: This became the public-health story of the step. Poison-centre incretin calls in 2033–34 ran ~2.3× the 2032 level, mostly from dosing errors: mislabelled strengths, tirzepatide or retatrutide sold as semaglutide, and severe hypoglycaemia in insulin users. In Oct 2033 the CDC traced a Mycobacterium abscessus outbreak to counterfeit 'generic semaglutide' pens: 231 confirmed cases in 14 states and 12 deaths, clustered in the Rio Grande Valley, Houston and Phoenix. There is no new pharmacological signal for authentic product.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Baseline enforcement continues: CDC Health Alert Network advisory, FDA warning letters (~90 in the window), CBP seizures and two further distributor indictments. No new statute, rule or programme.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
'Brain health' prescribing outside the label continues among 50–64-year-olds. The pill makes it easier, and the bone risk comes without proven cognitive benefit in that group.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling states population limits; no enforcement against off-label prescribing.

food_and_beverage.state: US packaged-food volume keeps falling ~2% a year. The decline slowed slightly because people pushed off employer coverage onto cheaper, less effective oral products eat a little more. Snack and confectionery brand sales to private equity continue. Protein, fibre and 'bone-and-muscle' formats grow. A new 'pill-day' format of small, high-protein breakfasts appears in grocery, because Foundayo has no fasting rule and the Wegovy pill does.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes fall for a sixth year. The orforglipron AUD label, ASAM first-line guidance and 'moderation dosing' push hardest on heavy-user volume, which carried a large share of sales. Craft breweries in Milwaukee, Asheville and Grand Rapids close or merge. Distillers lean on exports to markets where generic semaglutide is cheap and so also spreading. State excise forecasts carry an incretin line.

restaurants.state: Value chains keep closing units, especially where weight-only users moved to the less effective $149–199 oral tier. Fast casual standardises half plates. Border-region restaurants in McAllen and El Paso report shoppers combining a Mexican pharmacy run with lunch. Open Table suppers grow but have no measurable effect on sales.

apparel.state: Wide size runs are permanent. Uniform makers re-cut for military and police. Hip-protector apparel is normal in senior catalogues. Resale of 'before' sizes is a mature category.

fitness.state: Bridge referrals keep Medicare Advantage strength programmes and low-cost gyms busy. Employer retreat removed coaching-enrollment conditions, so referral-driven commercial memberships fell. Growth now comes from seniors and military, while working-age cash users train less.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend slows to ~+6%. Employers retreat from weight-only coverage to coded coverage plus 'direct access benefits'. The Seventh Circuit struck an outcomes-based premium differential under the ADA's voluntariness rule in 2033, the Fifth Circuit upheld one, and a cert petition is pending. PBMs sell coding-verification instead of adherence-verification.

pharma.state: Lilly is still the national champion and federal price setter. Novo regains volume with oral amycretin but its margins are squeezed by API duty and the high API load of oral peptides. Indian generic makers dominate global volume, and their US entry is stalled at one import-alerted plant. MDL reserves keep rising. Authentic-product sales lose an estimated 2.6M users to counterfeits.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now shows which tier you are in as much as whether you take the drug. A lean, muscled body with a coded prescription reads as covered. A body thinner than it was but holding steady reads as cash-pill. A body that has quickly regained reads as cut loose by the January 2034 plan change. After the outbreak, a heavier body refusing the drug on principle carries a new argument: at least I'm not injecting something from a parking lot.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 'Charlotte build' is still the upper-tier marker. The middle tier lives on the $149–199 oral products and looks it: moderately lighter, rarely sculpted. In the Rio Grande Valley, Hispanic working families in McAllen and Edinburg split between Reynosa pharmacy generics and the TrumpRx pill, and since October 2033 the choice carries fear. For older women in Sun City, posture and a fall-free year remain the class sign.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Open Table spread from church networks in Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa to Wichita and San Antonio, and in 2034 added memorial suppers for outbreak victims. Fat-liberation supper clubs in Oakland and Brooklyn grew again, with younger members who came of age on the drug. In households where adults take the pill, the family breakfast has come back, now as a pill-timing ritual.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule and sometimes the source ('legit only', 'Rx not Reynosa'). 'Drug-free' remains a value badge. Fewer couples negotiate around employer adherence windows because those windows mostly disappeared with employer coverage.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical for the covered and a household budget line for cash users. The backlash's 'hunger is how we were made' gained a public-health edge after the outbreak. A 'Made Hungry' rally in Nashville in May 2034 drew about 40,000 people. For many former heavy drinkers, appetite now means not wanting a drink, which the AUD label made respectable.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Validated excess anhedonia is ~3% overall (VA/PCORI 2033), concentrated at high doses. Survey 'reduced pleasure' is ~6–8% of long-term users, down from 10–15%. Dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~28%. The move from mainstream complaint to niche side effect had three mechanisms: switching from high-dose injectables to oral maintenance products; employer retreat removing the adherence gates that turned holidays into a workplace ritual; and the counterfeit story taking over the public attention. Low-dose Foundayo BED use is ≈1.3M, and its marketing dropped 'quiet' language after the AUD label reframed the product around cravings.
interior_life.framing: A side effect again, uncommon and dose-related. Clinicians manage it by stepping down to maintenance. 'The grey' survives as slang among long-term retatrutide users and in military counselling. Late-night jokes moved on to counterfeit pens.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employer-coordinated dose holidays are mostly gone with employer conditions. Sales staff no longer time holidays to quarter-end. Bridge and Medicaid-waiver users still manage PDC. Military and police programmes track tape and DEXA. Army chaplains still hear 'the grey', now mostly from soldiers on high-dose retatrutide.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' billings have shrunk back to a niche of club nights in Brooklyn and Austin. Festival 'holiday passes' quietly disappeared. Comedy moved from the grey to the pharmacy run in Reynosa. Sports-betting handle stopped falling as a share of incretin users moved to lower-intensity oral products.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists treat reward blunting as one possible cause among several, not the default. Dose holidays around conception remain routine because of pregnancy guidance, not because of the grey.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Candidates are no longer asked about holidays. They are asked where their constituents can buy safe product. The backlash coalition of religious, anti-pharma and fat-liberation groups used the outbreak to attack the whole system. Pro-access populists used it to demand the stalled generics. Neither got a law passed in this window.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and price-managing, but inactive. FDA approved the products under review (amycretin oral and injection, the orforglipron AUD supplement). Counterfeit enforcement ran at baseline (HAN advisory, warning letters, CBP seizures, indictments). No new rule, programme or statute followed the outbreak.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. The Bridge was extended unchanged by CR ($225/$50, conditional) through Sep 2035, and HRSA is flat at $5.0B. The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program and the ACA cessation mandate continue unchanged. The Strategic Supply Agreement still ties federal ceiling prices to Lilly's tariff exemption.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning persists in public programmes: Bridge continuation rules and the seven Medicaid adherence waivers. Employer conditioning largely dissolved through retreat rather than prohibition. The circuit split on wellness differentials is pending at the Supreme Court. Tennessee and Idaho premium-conditioning bans stand. HRSA remains unconditioned.
state.workforce_or_military: The Metabolic Readiness Program continues unchanged at ~150k active duty. Body-composition separations stay ~30% below the pre-programme baseline. Religious-accommodation requests reached ~2,600. FAA special issuance and big-city police and fire contracts are unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 duties on incretin API stand. A WTO panel on India's challenge was established in 2033 and has not reported. Novo absorbs duty while scaling oral API demand. Chinese amino-acid controls persist. API oversupply in India and China feeds both legitimate generics abroad and counterfeit supply chains into the US through Mexican courier routes that CBP mail seizures do not reach.

events.event: The settlement-licensed entry date for US generic semaglutide passes with no generic on shelves. The first filer's final approval is blocked by an FDA import alert on its API plant, which parks its 180-day exclusivity. Days later Novo cuts its TrumpRx semaglutide price to $199 and Lilly steps tirzepatide to $249.

FDA approves Novo's amycretin as a weekly injection and a daily tablet. The tablet showed 21.8% weight loss at 72 weeks, matching injectable tirzepatide. Novo lists it at $279 on TrumpRx and rations launch supply because oral peptide needs many times the API.

The CDC links a Mycobacterium abscessus outbreak to counterfeit 'generic semaglutide' pens sold in Rio Grande Valley flea markets and online: 231 cases in 14 states and 12 deaths. Open Table churches hold memorial suppers, and a 'Made Hungry' rally follows in Nashville in May 2034.

In open enrollment for 2034, several Fortune 100 employers and state employee plans drop weight-only incretin coverage and keep diabetes, cardiac, sleep-apnea and AUD codes. They offer a manufacturer portal link and an HSA top-up instead. A 2034 benefits survey finds weight-management coverage down to 49% of employers.

Congress extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge unchanged through September 2035 and flat-funds the HRSA incretin programme at $5.0B in a year-end continuing resolution. The $225 Bridge payment is left above the $199 cash price, and there is no counterfeit or generic provision.
FDA approves Foundayo (orforglipron) for alcohol use disorder. ASAM's guideline update lists GLP-1 drugs as a first-line option alongside naltrexone, following the 2033 VA/DoD guideline.

open_tensions: The generic vacuum: once the import alert on the first filer lifts, its parked exclusivity unlocks generic semaglutide at prices that would undercut the Strategic Supply Agreement ceilings. The federal price-setting bargain with Lilly and the $225 Bridge payment, already above the $199 cash price, would both have to be renegotiated by the September 2035 CR expiry.

Two-tier access has hardened. Coded patients pay copays, and weight-only patients pay $149–299 cash or go gray. The counterfeit outbreak struck the lower tier, but no agency or legislature has acted, and the backlash and pro-access blocs draw opposite lessons from the same deaths.

Users aged 65+ rose to ~13.7M on the dementia label and a needle-free pill, while modelled excess hip fractures climbed to ~20,500 a year. There are still no fracture-outcome data for oral amycretin or for antiresorptive cover in people over 75, and Bridge conditions are the only structured bone safeguard.

Employer conditioning dissolved through retreat, but Bridge and seven Medicaid waivers still rely on PBM adherence feeds degraded by skip-but-fill. The Supreme Court cert petition on wellness differentials, the unresolved Indiana disability challenge and the HRSA 'unconditioned' exception could each reopen the question of what an adherence condition may demand.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: Thirty Percent and Paying Cash: The Pill Caught Up, the Employers Walked Away, and the Fakes Moved In
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 almost one American adult in three, about eighty-three million people, is on an incretin drug. Growth has slowed. Two years ago ten new adults in every hundred had tried the drugs for the first time. This time it is between four and five. The rise in the total comes from restarters, from older people and from switching. The country did not run out of people who wanted the drug. It ran out of employers willing to pay for it.

The pill arrived first. In April 2033 the FDA approved Novo's amycretin as a daily tablet, and in its trial it took off about as much weight as a weekly tirzepatide shot. The needle had been the last argument for waiting, and it went. But an oral peptide needs far more raw ingredient than an injection, and Novo pays tariff on every gram it brings from Denmark. So the tablet launched at $279 a month and was rationed until supply caught up. Most of its three million users are switchers, not newcomers.

Prices kept falling the negotiated way. Semaglutide is $199 on the federal cash portal, tirzepatide $249 and retatrutide $299. The starter pills are $149 and stay there. The generic semaglutide that patent settlements had promised for March 2033 never reached a shelf. The first company in line had its ingredient plant put on an FDA import alert, and the law lets that company's exclusivity block everyone behind it. The date came and went.

In open enrollment that November, employers left. Large companies and state employee plans kept covering the drugs for diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea and drinking, and dropped coverage for weight alone. Instead they offered a link to the manufacturer portal and a small health-savings top-up. Fewer than half of employers now cover weight management. The result is two tiers. Patients with a diagnosis code pay a copay. Everyone else pays $149 to $299 a month, or goes elsewhere.

Elsewhere has grown to about thirteen million people. It includes compounders, Canadian websites, Indian courier parcels and above all the pharmacies across the bridge in Reynosa and Nuevo Progreso, where Mexican generic semaglutide costs less than a tank of gas. It also includes pens printed to look like the American generic everyone had heard was coming. In October 2033 the CDC traced a cluster of mycobacterial infections to those pens: 231 cases and twelve deaths, concentrated in the Rio Grande Valley. Poison-centre calls doubled, mostly from wrong doses. The authentic drugs carry no new warning. Washington issued advisories and warning letters and passed nothing. In December Congress extended the Medicare Bridge unchanged in a stopgap bill, which left Medicare paying $225 for a drug that costs $199 at the cash portal.

The backlash found its grief. Open Table churches in Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa held memorial suppers. In May some forty thousand people rallied in Nashville under the banner 'Made Hungry'. Fat-liberation supper clubs in Oakland are signing up members in their twenties who grew up watching their parents skip lunch.

The flatness people called 'the grey' has shrunk back into the label. Large veterans' and pragmatic studies found the real excess risk to be about three percent and mostly at high doses. Doctors now step patients down, and the employer adherence windows that turned dose holidays into a workplace ritual disappeared along with employer coverage. Comedians now joke about Reynosa instead.

In February 2034 the FDA approved the Foundayo pill for alcohol use disorder, and addiction guidelines now list these drugs alongside naltrexone. Spirits volumes are falling for a sixth year, and craft breweries in Milwaukee are merging to survive. In Sun City, older women still count a year without a fall as an achievement. Twenty-two percent of Americans over sixty-five are on a drug that may protect their memory while it thins their bones. The country looks leaner and calmer, and on the surface it looks in good order.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Treviño takes her Foundayo at 5:40 with coffee, because this pill doesn't care about food. Since January it costs $199 on the portal. The district plan dropped her Zepbound at New Year and kept her husband's, because Ruben has the diabetes code.

At Memorial Middle in McAllen she runs the cafeteria line. Eight hundred trays. Tacos al pastor, apples, milk. Lately the sixth-graders eat everything and the teachers take half portions. She clocks it the way she used to clock her own plate.

At lunch her phone buzzes. It's her sister Yesenia, who still drives to Reynosa every month for the real Mexican stuff in its sealed box, forty dollars. She has sent a photo of a bridge-line selfie with the caption 'legit, tranquila.' Marisol doesn't answer. Last November she went to Doña Licha's funeral, and the open sore on Licha's stomach had come from a pen with an American-looking label.

The scale in the nurse's office says she's up six pounds since January. The pill is gentler than the shot and weaker than the shot. She knows both things.

After work there's an Open Table supper in the fellowship hall at Sagrado Corazón. She goes because her mother goes. The priest says hunger is how we were made. A woman in a Made Hungry shirt passes the rice twice. Marisol takes a full plate and eats half.

At home Ruben does his shot at the counter, a five-dollar copay. She lines up tomorrow's pill beside the coffee maker and checks the portal. The amycretin tablet is $279 and in stock this month. She closes the app.
